sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Bad Homburg's parking policy has been a series of price moves rather than closures. The city's parking company, Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH, raised garage tariffs on 1 April 2023, taking one hour from €1.50 to €2.00 and three hours from €3.00 to €6.00, the first rise since January 2012. It said garages remained clearly cheaper than street parking at €3 an hour [0]. From 1 May 2024 it moved four garages to a continuous half-hour tariff, so a stay of 1 hour 20 minutes fell from €4.00 to €3.00 [2]. On the street, an amended fee ordinance in force from 1 September 2024 charges €0.40 per 10 minutes in the Ost, West and Thomasbrücke zones and €1.00 per 30 minutes in zone Süd and Horexstraße [3].

The city council adopted a mobility concept to 2035 with 51 measures on 21 March 2024 [5]. Its draft report found no serious capacity shortage. It reported average garage occupancy of 43% on 2016 counts against 64% on the street, and attributed the garage underuse partly to street tariffs having been cheaper than garage tariffs at the time, which it says has since been corrected [8]. A 2022 survey of passers-by rated the centre 2.1 overall but its parking options only 3 [18]. The report also describes a town shaped by commuting, with surveyed commuters travelling 27 km on average against a national 16.8 km [23]. Construction of the U2 extension from Gonzenheim to Bad Homburg station, about 1.6 km with 355 m in a tunnel, started in December 2025, with service targeted for 2029 at the latest [20].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: Recent changes are mostly to the garages' systems. In September 2026 the city published a tender to renew five of the Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH's parking systems and the Karstadt garage's, adding licence-plate recognition, QR codes, cashless web payment and self-service, installed during operation. That is a tender, with its deadline on 9 October 2026 [15]. The Seedammweg garage, with 405 spaces for the Taunus Therme and Seedammbad, reopened on 19 June 2026 after a major fire, reserved for spa guests, and part of it remains closed [16]. Permits for the Kurhaus and Rathaus garages are not being newly issued because of waiting lists, and the Parkhaus am Güterbahnhof offers a €50 a month commuter ticket for park-and-ride [13]. The Galeria department store is among 33 of the chain's 83 stores whose future is at risk, and no closure decision had been reported in July 2026 [17]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH operates seven garages and one car park, among ten garages and three decks or lots that the city lists for the centre and Kurpark, with a guidance system showing free spaces [10]. Its tariff overview gives capacities of 343 at the Kurhaus, 311 at the Schloss, 250 at the Rathaus, 326 at the Casino, 435 at Parkhaus am Bahnhof, 398 at the Güterbahnhof and 485 at Karstadt. It charges €1.00 per half hour with a €20 daily maximum in the Schloss, Rathaus and Karstadt garages, €1.50 an hour at the Casino and Güterbahnhof garages and €2 an hour at Parkhaus am Bahnhof [11].

Our data cover seven garages with 1,725 spaces, which are fewer than the city's own capacity figures, for example Karstadt at 300 against 485 and the Rathaus at 135 against 250, so percentages should be read with care. Four are within 500 m of the centre (1,038 spaces) and three more within 1 km. Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 24% on weekdays and 20% at weekends. The fullest is the Kurhausgarage (44% on weekdays, 35% at weekends), then the Rathausgarage (38%, dropping to 13% at weekends) and Louisen Arkaden (31%). Karstadt is at 25% and the Schloss at 21%. The garages by the station are almost empty: Am Bahnhof is at 15% and the Güterbahnhof, which sells park-and-ride permits at €50 a month, is at 2%. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Bad Homburg.
